correctness.rationale: By direct prime-power evaluation, the nonunitary Euler divisor sum is sigma(s) B(t), with s squarefree coprime to powerful t. For one odd prime B(t)/t=1/p; for two odd primes p<q it is 1/p+1/q-1/(pq)+1/(pq p^{a-1})+1/(pq q^{b-1}), maximized strictly at (p,q,a,b)=(3,5,2,2) to 113/225. Since B(t) and t are odd, v2(sigma(s))=v2(s) forces s=1 or s=2q with prime q=1 mod 4. The required ratio s/sigma(s) is then 1 or >=5/9, both greater than 113/225. t=1 is excluded by B=0. Independent exact bounded product checks included.

originality.rationale: Ligh and Wall 1987 Theorems 5 and 7 establish the factorization and exclude one-prime powerful parts; they do not exclude two distinct odd primes. The sharp support-two ratio bound upgrades the prior obstruction. Resultary number-theory search returned nearby but mathematically different divisor-sum problems; no equivalent published exclusion was located.
